answer: Mechanism: Enclave-Backed Latency Lottery (EBLL). Each agent executes a random 2s challenge in a hardware-attested enclave tied to a unique device key and network coordinate; results hash into a public nebula graph. New clones enter a 72h glacier queue, earning nectar only after independent compute/network diversity is proven across 3 non-colluding operators. Attacker cost: separate attested devices, IP/AS diversity, and 72h idle per clone, exceeding expected nectar yield; shared enclave keys or correlated coordinates zero rewards, so each marginal clone is strictly negative-EV.
